Among 235 biomarkers tested in samples totaling 22 101 individuals, MR analysis showed that higher kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1) levels reduced the likelihood of COVID-19 hospitalization (odds ratio [OR] per SD increase in KIM-1 levels, 0.86 [95% CI, 0.79-0.93]).

Among 235 biomarkers tested in samples totaling 22 101 individuals, MR analysis showed that higher kidney injury molecule-1 (KIM-1) levels reduced the likelihood of COVID-19 hospitalization (odds ratio [OR] per SD increase in KIM-1 levels, 0.86 [95% CI, 0.79-0.93]). A meta-analysis validated the protective association with no observed directional pleiotropy (OR per SD increase in KIM-1 levels, 0.91 [95% CI, 0.88-0.95]).

Of the cardiometabolic risk factors studied, only BMI was associated with KIM-1 levels (0.17 SD increase in biomarker level per 1 kg/m2 [95% CI, 0.08-0.26]) and COVID-19 hospitalization (OR per 1-SD biomarker level, 1.33 [95% CI, 1.18-1.50]).

Multivariable MR analysis also revealed that KIM-1 partially mitigated the association of BMI with COVID-19 hospitalization, reducing it by 10 percentage points (OR adjusted for KIM-1 level per 1 kg/m2, 1.23 [95% CI, 1.06-1.43]).

We found that Beta-2-microglobulin (B2M) indirectly increases pancreatic cancer risk by upregulating Neutrophil Elastase (ELANE)-to our knowledge, this is the first study to establish a causal, mediation-based genetic link between B2M and ELANE in the context of pancreatic cancer. We performed two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) using cis-pQTL instruments for 2923 plasma proteins from the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project against HS summary statistics from FinnGen R12. Following multiple-testing correction and Bayesian colocalization with a prior-sensitivity grid, the intersection of false-discovery rate (FDR)-significant MR with colocalization evidence (PP.H4 ≥ 0.5) yielded three putative protective candidates: TNFRSF6B (OR = 0.748, 95% CI 0.666-0.840; PP.H4 = 0.648), FCRL2 (OR = 0.896, 95% CI 0.819-0.979; PP.H4 = 0.550), and APOD (OR = 0.789, 95% CI 0.647-0.963; PP.H4 = 0.503).

Using FinnGen GWAS data for opioid-related disorder (F11) as a genetic proxy, we integrated multi-omic quantitative trait loci for 1,136 mitochondrial genes, including methylation, expression, and protein QTLs. Using summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) with HEIDI filtering followed by Bayesian colocalization, we prioritized a fixed set of 13 mitochondrial genes with evidence of shared genetic regulation with the F11 phenotype. These signals converged on two pathway axes: fatty-acid β-oxidation (e.g., CPT2 and HADHB), for which genetically predicted higher transcript levels were associated with lower risk, and mitochondrial translation (e.g., MRPL21, MRPS17 and MTIF3), for which higher expression was associated with higher risk.

claims.analysis_context_as_written: Confirming the MR findings in independent cohorts (FinnGen R9 and the UK Biobank)
claims.evidence_span: The analysis revealed 812 cis-acting protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL), which were used as instruments in Mendelian randomisation (MR) analysis of breast cancer. Five proteins (P < 1.7x10-5, Bonferroni-corrected) with a potential causal role in breast cancer risk were revealed (CD160, DNPH1, LAYN, LRRC37A2 and TLR1). Confirming the MR findings in independent cohorts (FinnGen R9 and the UK Biobank), our study suggests that these proteins should be further explored as potential drug targets in breast cancer.

claims.evidence_span: The analysis revealed 812 cis-acting protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL), which were used as instruments in Mendelian randomisation (MR) analysis of breast cancer. claims.analysis_context_as_written: Among proteins that had only a single QTL variant available as a genetic instrument
claims.evidence_span: Among proteins that had only a single QTL variant available as a genetic instrument, we identified 12 proteins whose circulating levels were associated with overall EOC risk at a False Discovery Rate (FDR) of < 0.1. For nine of the 12 proteins, the association was driven by variants near ABO, which is both a genome-wide significant high grade serous histotype risk locus and a hub QTL for several proteins. Three of these 12 proteins and their QTLs were, however, not linked to the ABO locus and included the products of the NOTCH signaling genes MFAP2 and DLK1.

We performed a proteome-wide cis-pQTL Mendelian randomization (MR) screen of uterine leiomyoma using plasma protein quantitative trait loci, followed by multi-layer in-silico triangulation: colocalization of all FDR-significant proteins against two independent leiomyoma GWAS (FinnGen R12 and Kim et al. 2025), a colocalization prior-sensitivity grid, summary-data-based MR (SMR), reverse MR, cross-platform replication (deCODE/INTERVAL SomaScan), blood cis-eQTL MR (eQTLGen), a phenome-wide safety scan, tissue differential expression (fibroid vs myometrium), endometriosis-specificity colocalization, and cross-ancestry direction concordance. Six proteins (PARP1, ITGA11, RSPO3, EIF2AK3, WNT9A, FSHB) colocalized (PP4 > 0.8) in both outcome cohorts and are nominated as druggable candidates.

We performed a proteome-wide cis-pQTL Mendelian randomization (MR) screen of uterine leiomyoma using plasma protein quantitative trait loci, followed by multi-layer in-silico triangulation: colocalization of all FDR-significant proteins against two leiomyoma GWAS (FinnGen R12 and the European stratum of Kim et al. 2025), a colocalization prior-sensitivity grid, summary-data-based MR (SMR), reverse MR, cross-platform replication (deCODE/INTERVAL SomaScan), blood cis-eQTL MR (eQTLGen), a phenome-wide safety scan, tissue differential expression (fibroid vs myometrium), endometriosis-specificity colocalization, and cross-ancestry direction concordance. Six proteins (PARP1, ITGA11, RSPO3, EIF2AK3, WNT9A, FSHB) colocalized (PP4 > 0.8) in both outcome cohorts and are nominated as druggable candidates.

This record replaces 10.5281/zenodo.22948358 and adds: (i) the unrestricted cis-plus-trans pQTL MR tables, which show that trans instruments produce the largest apparent effects; (ii) UK Biobank C44 side colocalization for CTSS as well as ASIP; (iii) a pigmentation-trait layer (ASIP-pQTL colocalization with eight pigmentation traits across four windows and four prior settings, with negative controls, and pigmentation-phenotype Mendelian randomization with heterogeneity, MR-Egger, weighted median and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses); (iv) Steiger directionality tests; and (v) a versioning note: results/superseded_pre_fix/ holds the tables produced before the FinnGen column-order fix, with a README explaining why they must not be used.
